1.explanation: This minimal server demonstrates the Lighthouse bug: the parent page includes an iframe whose document is intentionally large and delivery is network-throttled. When Lighthouse audits `/index.html`, it does not include the iframe’s network and rendering cost in the parent’s metrics. Running Lighthouse directly against `/huge-dom.html` shows the true slow performance. The disparity reproduces the misleading higher score on the parent page.
1.bug_scenario: When you load a page that simply embeds a slow, large-DOM iframe, Lighthouse’s performance score on the *parent* page remains high (around 70), even though the iframe itself on its own scores very poorly (around 40) when you run Lighthouse directly against it. In other words, Lighthouse is ignoring the cost of the iframe when it audits the parent page, resulting in a misleadingly good score for the parent.
